newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso extends slide on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso extends slide on dollar short-covering.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended its opening slide in mid-morning trade on Tuesday due to demand to cover short dollar positions and rises in U.S. long bond yields, traders said.
"The peso usually weakens at year's end to close dollar positions," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were two and 2.6 centavos weaker at 7.8750/7.8770 and 7.8690/7.8740 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts meanwhile closed 1.9 centavos weaker at 7.8610/7.8640 per dollar.

Also weighing on the peso was a sharp rise in the U.S. long bond yield. The yield jumped to 6.64 percent this morning after closing at 6.54 percent Monday. A 14.2 percent rise in U.S. new home sales for November caused the sell-off in Treasury prices.
